title: Genome-wide identification and classification of transcription factors in plant genomes
text: Transcription factors (TFs) proteins bind cis-regulatory elements promoter regions genes regulate expression. Identifying genome useful variety reasons, exploring evolutionary history across clades inferring gene regulatory networks. planttfhunter allows users identify plant TFs whole-genome protein sequences classify families subfamilies (applicable) using classification schemes implemented PlantTFDB TAPscan, well structure-based families, classes, superclasses Plant-TFClass. planttfhunter interoperates core Bioconductor packages (.e., AAStringSet objects input, SummarizedExperiment objects output), can easily incorporated pipelines TF identification classification large-scale genomic data sets.

title: Genome-wide identification and classification of transcription factors in plant genomes
text: TF identification classification based presence signature protein domains, identified using profile hidden Markov models (HMMs). Three classification schemes available: PlantTFDB (Jin et al. 2017): TFs classified families subfamilies based DNA-binding, auxiliary, forbidden domains. TAPscan v4 (Petroll et al. 2025): transcription-associated proteins (TAPs), include TFs, transcriptional regulators (TRs), putative TAPs (PTs), classified 130 families based rules specifying domains family . Domain hits identified using gathering thresholds domain-specific coverage cutoffs. planttfhunter uses R implementation TAPscan’s original Perl script, reproduces results original implementation. Plant-TFClass (Blanc-Mathieu et al. 2024): TFs classified families, classes, superclasses based 3D structure DNA-binding domains. Plant-TFClass classifications inferred TAPscan classifications using correspondence table two systems. TAPscan families correspond one Plant-TFClass family (e.g., TAPscan’s AP2 family includes Plant-TFClass’s AP2, ERF/DREB, RAV families). cases, PlantTFDB subfamilies used resolve ambiguity, possible (e.g., gene classified PlantTFDB), possible classifications reported, separated ‘;’. schemes, classification levels without specific level filled name general level. example, PlantTFDB family bHLH subfamilies, subfamily also bHLH, Plant-TFClass class GRAS families, family also GRAS. classification schemes available data sets package, can see (click expand). Genes assigned family (subfamily, ) domains column none domains column Should_not. Numbers parentheses indicate required number copies domain. TAPscan families/subfamilies multiple rows correspond one Plant-TFClass family, PlantTFDB subfamily gene (column PlantTFDB_subfamily) used choose among .

HMMER program (Finn et al. 2011) used scan protein sequences presence DNA-binding protein domains, well auxiliary forbidden domains. Pre-built HMM profiles can found extdata/ directory package. multicore machine, can speed HMMER searches increasing number threads argument threads. can run annotate_domains() 2: Now TF-related domains, can classify TFs families function classify_tfs(). output contains one row per gene, genes classified one schemes NA respective columns. Plant-TFClass classifications inferred TAPscan classifications, TAPscan annotation required obtain . TAPscan’s scheme also includes transcription-associated proteins (e.g., transcriptional regulators), genes usually classified TAPscan. interested single classification scheme, can use argument scheme get classifications scheme. TAPscan, class family (TF, TR, PT) indicated column TAP_class. TAP classes, well descriptions references TAPscan family, available data set tap_class.

what: Counting TFs per family in multiple species at once
title: Genome-wide identification and classification of transcription factors in plant genomes
text: want get TF counts per family multiple species, can use function get_tf_counts(). function takes named list data frames TF classifications species (returned classify_tfs()) input, returns SummarizedExperiment object containing TF counts per family species, well species metadata (optional). familiar SummarizedExperiment class, consider checking vignettes SummarizedExperiment Bioconductor package. real data sets, first identify classify TFs species. instance, list AAStringSet objects proteomes multiple species 3, run: demonstrate get_tf_counts() works, simulate TF classifications 4 species sampling 100 random genes TF classifications obtained (gsu_families) 4 times. Now, let’s also create simulated species metadata data frame “species”. can add many columns want species metadata data frame, make sure species names row names, names(families) match rownames(species_metadata), otherwise get_tf_counts() return error. Now list TF classifications species metadata, can execute get_tf_counts(). default, TFs counted per PlantTFDB family, can choose schemes argument scheme, classification levels argument level. Possible levels ‘family’ ‘subfamily’ PlantTFDB TAPscan, ‘superclass’, ‘class’, ‘family’ Plant-TFClass. counting TFs levels highest level scheme (e.g., subfamilies), rowData output contains higher levels row, can use aggregate counts. example PlantTFDB subfamilies: Since get_tf_counts() takes classification tables input, can also filter counting. example, can get counts TAPscan TFs (excluding TRs PTs) per subfamily: Finally, can get TF counts per Plant-TFClass superclass: Cool, huh? real-world analyses, TF counts per family multiple species obtained get_tf_counts(), can try find associations TF counts eco-evolutionary aspects traits species (e.g., higher frequencies stress-related TF family species inhabits stressful environment).
code: families <- lapply(proteomes, function(x) classify_tfs(annotate_domains(x))) set.seed(123) # for reproducibility  # Simulate 4 different species by sampling 100 random genes  families <- list(     Gsu1 = gsu_families[sample(nrow(gsu_families), 100), ],     Gsu2 = gsu_families[sample(nrow(gsu_families), 100), ],     Gsu3 = gsu_families[sample(nrow(gsu_families), 100), ],     Gsu4 = gsu_families[sample(nrow(gsu_families), 100), ] ) # Create simulated species metadata species_metadata <- data.frame(     row.names = names(families),     Division = "Rhodophyta",     Origin = c("US", "Belgium", "China", "Brazil") )  species_metadata #>        Division  Origin #> Gsu1 Rhodophyta      US #> Gsu2 Rhodophyta Belgium #> Gsu3 Rhodophyta   China #> Gsu4 Rhodophyta  Brazil # Get TF counts per PlantTFDB family in each species tf_counts <- get_tf_counts(families, species_metadata)  # Take a look at the SummarizedExperiment object tf_counts #> class: SummarizedExperiment  #> dim: 14 4  #> metadata(0): #> assays(1): counts #> rownames(14): bHLH bZIP ... NF-Y Nin-like #> rowData names(0): #> colnames(4): Gsu1 Gsu2 Gsu3 Gsu4 #> colData names(2): Division Origin  # Look at the matrix of counts: assay() function from SummarizedExperiment SummarizedExperiment::assay(tf_counts) #>                 Gsu1 Gsu2 Gsu3 Gsu4 #> bHLH               1    0    2    0 #> bZIP               5    7    7    5 #> C2C2               5    9    8    6 #> C2H2               3    0    2    4 #> C3H                4    6    5    3 #> CPP                2    0    2    1 #> E2F/DP             2    3    1    8 #> GARP               1    0    2    0 #> HSF                3    2    2    2 #> MADS               0    1    1    0 #> MYB superfamily   16   14   15   16 #> NF-X1              1    0    0    1 #> NF-Y               3    4    5    5 #> Nin-like           3    2    4    6  # Look at the species metadata: colData() function from SummarizedExperiment SummarizedExperiment::colData(tf_counts) #> DataFrame with 4 rows and 2 columns #>         Division      Origin #>      <character> <character> #> Gsu1  Rhodophyta          US #> Gsu2  Rhodophyta     Belgium #> Gsu3  Rhodophyta       China #> Gsu4  Rhodophyta      Brazil # Get TF counts per PlantTFDB subfamily subfam_counts <- get_tf_counts(     families, scheme = "PlantTFDB", level = "subfamily" )  # Look at the family of each subfamily head(SummarizedExperiment::rowData(subfam_counts)) #> DataFrame with 6 rows and 1 column #>         PlantTFDB_family #>              <character> #> bHLH                bHLH #> bZIP                bZIP #> C2H2                C2H2 #> C3H                  C3H #> CO-like             C2C2 #> CPP                  CPP # Keep only TFs in TAPscan classifications tapscan_tfs <- lapply(families, function(x) x[x$TAP_class %in% "TF", ])  # Get TF counts per TAPscan subfamily tapscan_counts <- get_tf_counts(     tapscan_tfs, scheme = "TAPscan", level = "subfamily" ) head(SummarizedExperiment::assay(tapscan_counts)) #>           Gsu1 Gsu2 Gsu3 Gsu4 #> ARID         0    3    2    1 #> bHLH         1    0    2    0 #> bZIP         5    9    9    6 #> C2C2_GATA    3    5    6    3 #> C2H2         3    0    1    4 #> C3H          4    6    3    3 # Get TF counts per Plant-TFClass superclass superclass_counts <- get_tf_counts(     families, scheme = "PlantTFClass", level = "superclass" ) SummarizedExperiment::assay(superclass_counts) #>                                             Gsu1 Gsu2 Gsu3 Gsu4 #> Alpha-helices exposed by beta-structures       0    1    1    0 #> Basic domains                                  6    9   11    6 #> Helix-turn-helix domains                      26   24   25   33 #> Other all-alpha-helical DNA-binding domains    0    2    2    3 #> Yet undefined DNA-binding domains              2    0    2    1 #> Zinc-coordinating DNA-binding domains          6    5    7    7

planttfhunter 1.13.1
text: release adds two new classification schemes (TAPscan Plant-TFClass) redesigns API around simpler workflow: annotate_domains() -> classify_tfs() -> get_tf_counts(). NEW FEATURES TFs can now classified using classification scheme TAPscan v4 (Petroll et al., 2025), addition PlantTFDB’s scheme. TAPscan classification algorithm (tapscan_classify.pl v4.76, rules v82 coverage values v11) ported R reproduces results original Perl implementation. TAPscan classifications include variable TAP_class indicating whether family contains transcription factors (TF), transcriptional regulators (TR), putative TAPs (PT). TFs also classified superclasses, classes, families structure-based classification Plant-TFClass (Blanc-Mathieu et al., 2024). Plant-TFClass classifications inferred TAPscan classifications using correspondence table two systems. TAPscan subfamily corresponds one Plant-TFClass family (TAPscan’s AP2, ABI3/VP1, MADS), PlantTFDB subfamilies used resolve ambiguity; possible, possible classifications reported, separated ‘;’. PlantTFDB classifications now include families (e.g., AP2/ERF) subfamilies (e.g., ERF), PlantTFDB’s classification scheme. New function annotate_domains() annotate sequences domains used PlantTFDB TAPscan. threads argument run HMMER multiple threads. New data sets tapscan_scheme (TAPscan’s classification rules), planttfclass_scheme (correspondence TAPscan Plant-TFClass), tap_class (classes, descriptions, references TAPscan families). BREAKING CHANGES annotate_pfam() replaced annotate_domains(), returns list two data frames (PlantTFDB TAPscan) variables Gene, Domain, qlen, c_evalue, hmm_from, hmm_to. classify_tfs() now takes output annotate_domains() input (data frames returned annotate_pfam() longer accepted), returns data frame one row per gene variables Gene, PlantTFDB_family, PlantTFDB_subfamily, TAPscan_family, TAPscan_subfamily, TAP_class, PlantTFClass_superclass, PlantTFClass_class, PlantTFClass_family. Note classifications previously reported variable Family (e.g., ERF) now PlantTFDB_subfamily, PlantTFDB_family contains PlantTFDB families (e.g., AP2/ERF). Genes assigned one PlantTFDB family families (subfamilies) separated ‘;’. get_tf_counts() now takes named list data frames TF classifications (returned classify_tfs()) input, instead list AAStringSet objects. way, domains annotated , TFs can counted different ways (filtered, needed) without running HMMER . default, TFs counted per PlantTFDB family (previously, PlantTFDB subfamily). Data set classification_scheme renamed planttfdb_scheme, names ‘M_type’, ‘MYB_related’, ‘LBD (AS2/LOB)’ changed ‘M-type’, ‘MYB-related’, ‘LBD’, respectively, match output classify_tfs(). Data sets gsu_families tf_counts removed, can obtained milliseconds classify_tfs(gsu_annotation) get_tf_counts(), respectively. Data sets gsu gsu_annotation updated. BUG FIXES HD-ZIP (via HD-ZIP_I/II), TALE (via BELL), WOX TFs never identified, names domains match names profile HMMs. TFs classified HB-. Trihelix STAT TFs never identified reason. Genes two B-box domains CCT domain classified CO-like DBB. now classified CO-like . get_tf_counts() returned error species names alphabetical order, reorder species metadata match order species count matrix.
